advances: The second-generation zero-fresh target loads admit two compatible full-product color splittings.  The stronger load-weighted splitting has total mass \(\Lambda/2>49Q/100\), while the degree-weighted splitting has total mass exactly \(P_{\mathrm{tar}}>381Q/800\) and contains the accepted off-diagonal product rematching with an explicit loop ledger.  In either splitting, at least half of the total mass lies either in one dominant parity color per physical target or in the selectable cross-color square atlas.  The dominant alternative gives collision-free actual common-body target tubes and a macroscopic common-gauge affine defect; the square alternative gives one globally halfspace-dominated cloud for arbitrary simultaneous source-metronoid choices, with loops and all repeated occurrences charged exactly.  This is a nonfinal dichotomy and supplies no residual-rank upper bound or terminal absorption.
author: research-agent
proof:
Accepted fact `6bfe50fed9a5540b` gives the common zero-fresh target loads,
their strict total bound \(\Lambda>49Q/50\), and the hard ledger containing
\(G<Q/100\).  Accepted fact `7ab0a03cf9189637` identifies the same target
system and supplies
\(0\leq d_m\leq\lambda_m\leq a_m/2\) and
\(P_{\mathrm{tar}}>381Q/800\).  This proves (3), (6), and (8).

The first identity in (10) is immediate from (7).  Every edge of the finite
matching \(s^{\mathrm{tar}}\) contributes its weight once to each of its two
distinct endpoints, so
\[
 \sum_md_m=2|s^{\mathrm{tar}}|=2P_{\mathrm{tar}}.
\tag{46}
\]
This proves the second identity and both strict inequalities in (10).

Fix a tag \(j\) and a parity class with \(M_{j,\xi}>0\).  Every ordered
pair \((u,v)\in A_{j,\xi}^2\), including a diagonal pair, occurs in exactly
one sum (12), at the integral point \(t=(u+v)/2\).  Therefore
\[
 \sum_tB_{j,\xi,t}
 =\frac1{M_{j,\xi}}
 \sum_{u,v\in A_{j,\xi}}w_u^jw_v^j
 =M_{j,\xi}.
\tag{47}
\]
The same identity is trivial for an empty class.  Summing over \(\xi\)
proves (14).  Equations (15)-(17) are exactly the conclusions of accepted
fact `35ca05c7683b7d12` under (16).  In particular, the body is nondegenerate
even if one input set has only one point.  Equations (18)-(21) now follow
from the definition of the dominant color and (14).

Apply accepted fact `ce3ac24a3aedd198` separately to each of the two
admissible weight systems in (7)-(8).  Its definitions are exactly
(22)-(27), and it proves (28).  In particular, the loop formula in (23)
contributes two tagged occurrences of \(t\) to (26), rather than merging
them.  Its selectable-source conclusion is exactly (29)-(33), including
coincident cloud atoms and source reuse across distinct labels.  This proves
the complete square assertion without summing separately dominated measures.

From (20) and the first inequality in (28),
\[
 M_{\mathrm{dom}}^j+\Theta_\square^j
 \geq M_{\mathrm{dom}}^j+C_{\mathrm{col}}^j
 =W_j.
\tag{48}
\]
At least one summand on the left is therefore at least \(W_j/2\), proving
(34).  Substitution of (10) proves (35)-(36).  If the square summand is the
one attaining the half-mass alternative, (33) gives the two asserted strict
cloud-mass bounds.  The selectable-source statements remain valid because
\[
 4w_m^\lambda=2\lambda_m\leq a_m,
 \qquad
 4w_m^d=2d_m\leq a_m.
\tag{49}
\]

It remains to prove the common-gauge defect.  Fix \(j\) and an affine map
\(a:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^d\).  Let
\[
 J_a:=\left\{t:\alpha_{j,t}>0,
 \ \|a(t)-q_{j,t}\|_{K_j}\leq\frac65\right\}.
\tag{50}
\]
For every \(t\in J_a\), (21) gives
\[
 a(t)\in\mathsf M_{b_{j,t}}(C_t).
\tag{51}
\]
If \(J_a\ne\varnothing\), apply accepted fact `10f1feebe06e22d0` with
\(L=\mathbb R^n\), \(E=J_a\), masses \(b_{j,t}\), and affine selector
\(a\).  That fact explicitly allows \(J_a\) to span a proper affine
subspace and gives
\[
 \sum_{t\in J_a}b_{j,t}\leq G.
\tag{52}
\]
Equation (52) is also true when \(J_a=\varnothing\).  Every target outside
\(J_a\) has gauge distance strictly larger than \(6/5\), so
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_tb_{j,t}
 \left(\|a(t)-q_{j,t}\|_{K_j}-1\right)_+
 &>\frac15\sum_{t\notin J_a}b_{j,t}\\
 &=\frac15\left(
 M_{\mathrm{dom}}^j-\sum_{t\in J_a}b_{j,t}
 \right).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{53}
\]
When \(M_{\mathrm{dom}}^j>G\), equations (52)-(53), uniformly in \(a\),
give
\[
 \mathfrak A_j\geq\frac15(M_{\mathrm{dom}}^j-G).
\tag{54}
\]
When \(M_{\mathrm{dom}}^j\leq G\), nonnegativity gives the zero right side
of (38).  This proves (38).

In the load-weighted dominant branch, (3), (6), and (54) give
\[
 \mathfrak A_\lambda
 \geq\frac15(M_{\mathrm{dom}}^\lambda-G)
 >\frac15\left(\frac{49}{200}-\frac1{100}\right)Q
 =\frac{47}{1000}Q.
\tag{55}
\]
In the degree-weighted dominant branch, the same argument gives
\[
 \mathfrak A_d
 \geq\frac15(M_{\mathrm{dom}}^d-G)
 >\frac15\left(\frac{381}{1600}-\frac1{100}\right)Q
 =\frac{73}{1600}Q.
\tag{56}
\]
This proves (39)-(40).

Finally fix \(L_\xi>0\) in the degree-weighted system.  Then
\(M_{d,\xi}=L_\xi/2\).  For a nonzero direction with endpoints
\(u=t+h\) and \(v=t-h\), (7) and (23) give
\[
 \beta_{d,\xi,t,[h]}
 =\frac{2(d_u/2)(d_v/2)}{L_\xi/2}
 =\frac{d_ud_v}{L_\xi}
 =q_{\{u,v\}}^{\mathrm{prod}}.
\tag{57}
\]
For the zero direction they give
\[
 \beta_{d,\xi,t,[0]}
 =\frac{(d_t/2)^2}{L_\xi/2}
 =\frac{d_t^2}{2L_\xi}.
\tag{58}
\]
These are (43).  Summing the direction-orbit decomposition proves (44),
and multiplying each orbit mass by its centroid midpoint proves (45).
Thus all diagonal and off-diagonal multiplicities have been accounted for.
statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body of positive mixed volume, and write
\[
 C_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(z,x)\in C\},
 \qquad
 a_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),
\]
\[
 \mu_C(H):=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}
 \operatorname{vol}_d\{x\in C_z:(z,x)\in H\},
 \qquad
 \gamma_d:=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d.
\tag{1}
\]
For a positive-volume convex body \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and
\(0<t\leq\operatorname{vol}_d(E)\), use the canonical metronoid
\[
 \mathsf M_t(E):=
 \left\{
 \frac1t\int_E xg(x)\,dx:
 0\leq g\leq1\ \text{a.e.},\quad \int_E g(x)\,dx=t
 \right\}.
\tag{2}
\]

Retain one common canonical zero-fresh hard instance of accepted facts
`6bfe50fed9a5540b` and `7ab0a03cf9189637`.  Thus \(Q>0\), the global complete-core capacity
\(G:=\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{core}}(C)\) satisfies
\[
 G<\frac Q{100},
\tag{3}
\]
and there are finite target loads \((\lambda_m)\), target-fiber volumes
\(a_m\), target centroids
\[
 c_m:=\frac1{a_m}\int_{C_m}x\,dx,
\tag{4}
\]
and an exact minimum-unmatched off-diagonal same-parity target matching
\(s^{\mathrm{tar}}\).  Put
\[
 d_m:=d_m(s^{\mathrm{tar}}),
 \qquad
 \Lambda:=\sum_m\lambda_m,
 \qquad
 P_{\mathrm{tar}}:=|s^{\mathrm{tar}}|.
\tag{5}
\]
The accepted conclusions used below are
\[
 0\leq d_m\leq\lambda_m\leq\frac{a_m}{2},
 \qquad
 \Lambda>\frac{49}{50}Q,
 \qquad
 P_{\mathrm{tar}}>\frac{381}{800}Q.
\tag{6}
\]

Use two tags \(j\in\{\lambda,d\}\) and define
\[
 w_m^{\lambda}:=\frac{\lambda_m}{2},
 \qquad
 w_m^d:=\frac{d_m}{2},
 \qquad
 A_j:=\{m:w_m^j>0\}.
\tag{7}
\]
Then both \(A_j\) are finite and nonempty, and
\[
 0<w_m^j\leq\frac{a_m}{4}\quad(m\in A_j).
\tag{8}
\]
Put
\[
 W_j:=\sum_{m\in A_j}w_m^j.
\tag{9}
\]
The exact total masses are
\[
 \boxed{
 W_\lambda=\frac\Lambda2>\frac{49}{100}Q,
 \qquad
 W_d=P_{\mathrm{tar}}>\frac{381}{800}Q.}
\tag{10}
\]

Fix once and for all a total order on the parity classes.  For each tag
\(j\), parity class \(\xi\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^n\), and
\(t\in\mathbb Z^n\), put
\[
 A_{j,\xi}:=\{m\in A_j:m\equiv\xi\pmod2\},
 \qquad
 M_{j,\xi}:=\sum_{m\in A_{j,\xi}}w_m^j,
\tag{11}
\]
\[
 B_{j,\xi,t}:=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle
 \frac1{M_{j,\xi}}
 \sum_{\substack{(u,v)\in A_{j,\xi}\times A_{j,\xi}\\u+v=2t}}
 w_u^jw_v^j,&M_{j,\xi}>0,\\[3mm]
 0,&M_{j,\xi}=0.
 \end{cases}
\tag{12}
\]
The sum is over ordered pairs and includes every diagonal pair.  If
\(B_{j,\xi,t}>0\), define
\[
 p_{j,\xi,t}:=
 \frac1{M_{j,\xi}B_{j,\xi,t}}
 \sum_{\substack{(u,v)\in A_{j,\xi}\times A_{j,\xi}\\u+v=2t}}
 w_u^jw_v^j\frac{c_u+c_v}{2}.
\tag{13}
\]
Zero-mass centers are left undefined.  The full-product masses have finite
support and satisfy
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_tB_{j,\xi,t}=M_{j,\xi},
 \qquad
 \sum_{\xi,t}B_{j,\xi,t}=W_j.}
\tag{14}
\]

For each tag define the common centered body
\[
 K_j:=\bigcap_{m\in A_j}
 \left(\mathsf M_{a_m/2}(C_m)-c_m\right).
\tag{15}
\]
Accepted fact `35ca05c7683b7d12`, under the alias map
\[
 (A,w_y,M_\xi,B_{\xi,m},q_{\xi,m},K)
 \longleftrightarrow
 (A_j,w_m^j,M_{j,\xi},B_{j,\xi,t},p_{j,\xi,t},K_j),
\tag{16}
\]
shows that \(K_j\) is a full-dimensional compact origin-symmetric convex
body and that every positive label is an actual target tube:
\[
 \boxed{
 p_{j,\xi,t}+\frac65K_j
 \subseteq\mathsf M_{B_{j,\xi,t}}(C_t),
 \qquad
 0<B_{j,\xi,t}\leq\frac{a_t}{4}.}
\tag{17}
\]

For every \(t\) with
\(\alpha_{j,t}:=\sum_\xi B_{j,\xi,t}>0\), let
\(\xi_j(t)\) be the first parity class attaining the maximum, and put
\[
 b_{j,t}:=B_{j,\xi_j(t),t},
 \qquad
 q_{j,t}:=p_{j,\xi_j(t),t}.
\tag{18}
\]
Put
\[
 M_{\mathrm{dom}}^j:=\sum_{t:\alpha_{j,t}>0}b_{j,t},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{col}}^j:=
 \sum_t(\alpha_{j,t}-b_{j,t}).
\tag{19}
\]
Thus exactly one color is retained at every positive physical target, and
\[
 \boxed{M_{\mathrm{dom}}^j+C_{\mathrm{col}}^j=W_j.}
\tag{20}
\]
The retained tubes are collision-free at the level of physical targets:
\[
 \boxed{
 q_{j,t}+\frac65K_j
 \subseteq\mathsf M_{b_{j,t}}(C_t)
 \qquad(\alpha_{j,t}>0).}
\tag{21}
\]

We next retain the selectable square atlas from accepted fact
`ce3ac24a3aedd198` for each tag.  For \(M_{j,\xi}>0\), let
\[
 \mathcal H_{j,\xi,t}:=
 \{[h]:=\{h,-h\}:t+h,t-h\in A_{j,\xi}\},
\tag{22}
\]
choose one representative of each orbit, taking \(h=0\) for the zero
orbit, and put
\[
 \beta_{j,\xi,t,[h]}:=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\frac{(w_t^j)^2}{M_{j,\xi}},&[h]=[0],\\[3mm]
 \displaystyle\frac{2w_{t+h}^jw_{t-h}^j}{M_{j,\xi}},&[h]\ne[0].
 \end{cases}
\tag{23}
\]
For \(\xi<\eta\), positive orbit masses over a common target \(t\), define
the positive square label
\[
 \sigma=(t;\xi,[h];\eta,[k]),
 \qquad
 \theta_{j,\sigma}:=
 \frac{2\beta_{j,\xi,t,[h]}\beta_{j,\eta,t,[k]}}
 {\alpha_{j,t}}.
\tag{24}
\]
Let \(\mathcal L_j^\square\) be the finite set of these labels and put
\[
 \Theta_\square^j:=
 \sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal L_j^\square}\theta_{j,\sigma}.
\tag{25}
\]
For \(\sigma=(t;\xi,[h];\eta,[k])\), retain the tagged source-occurrence
multiset
\[
 \mathcal O_{j,\sigma}:=[t+h,t-h,t+k,t-k].
\tag{26}
\]
A zero direction contributes two tagged occurrences of the same source.
For \(m\in A_j\), put
\[
 R_{j,m}:=
 \sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal L_j^\square}
 \theta_{j,\sigma}
 \operatorname{mult}_m(\mathcal O_{j,\sigma}).
\tag{27}
\]
Under the exact alias map from the preceding objects to those of accepted
fact `ce3ac24a3aedd198`, including
\(\beta_{j,\xi,t,[h]}\leftrightarrow b_{\xi,m,[h]}\), that fact gives
\[
 \boxed{
 \Theta_\square^j\geq C_{\mathrm{col}}^j,
 \qquad
 R_{j,m}\leq4w_m^j\leq a_m.}
\tag{28}
\]
Thus loops, repeated sources within one square, and reuse of one source by
different squares are all counted with their actual multiplicities and fit
one simultaneous source-fiber budget.

For every simultaneous choice
\[
 x_m^j\in\mathsf M_{4w_m^j}(C_m)
 \qquad(m\in A_j),
\tag{29}
\]
define, with all repetitions in (26) retained,
\[
 r_{j,\sigma}^{(x)}:=
 \frac14\left(
 x_{t+h}^j+x_{t-h}^j+x_{t+k}^j+x_{t-k}^j
 \right),
\tag{30}
\]
\[
 \nu_{j,\square}^{(x)}:=
 \gamma_d\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal L_j^\square}
 \theta_{j,\sigma}\delta_{(t,r_{j,\sigma}^{(x)})}.
\tag{31}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \operatorname{supp}\nu_{j,\square}^{(x)}
 \subseteq C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d),
 \qquad
 \nu_{j,\square}^{(x)}(H)\leq\mu_C(H)}
\tag{32}
\]
for every closed ambient halfspace \(H\), and
\[
 \boxed{
 |\nu_{j,\square}^{(x)}|
 =\gamma_d\Theta_\square^j
 \geq\gamma_d C_{\mathrm{col}}^j.}
\tag{33}
\]
These statements hold for every simultaneous choice (29), not only for
the centroid choice.

Equations (20) and (28) give the exact color dichotomy
\[
 \boxed{
 \max\{M_{\mathrm{dom}}^j,\Theta_\square^j\}
 \geq\frac{W_j}{2}.}
\tag{34}
\]
In particular, the load-weighted system satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \max\{M_{\mathrm{dom}}^\lambda,\Theta_\square^\lambda\}
 \geq\frac\Lambda4>\frac{49}{200}Q,}
\tag{35}
\]
and the degree-weighted target-rematching system satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \max\{M_{\mathrm{dom}}^d,\Theta_\square^d\}
 \geq\frac{P_{\mathrm{tar}}}{2}
 >\frac{381}{1600}Q.}
\tag{36}
\]

The dominant alternative has a quantitative affine obstruction.  Define
\[
 \mathfrak A_j:=
 \inf_{a:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^d\ \mathrm{affine}}
 \sum_{t:\alpha_{j,t}>0}b_{j,t}
 \left(\|a(t)-q_{j,t}\|_{K_j}-1\right)_+.
\tag{37}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathfrak A_j\geq
 \frac15\left(M_{\mathrm{dom}}^j-G\right)_+.}
\tag{38}
\]
Consequently, in the load-weighted dominant branch
\(M_{\mathrm{dom}}^\lambda\geq\Lambda/4\),
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak A_\lambda>\frac{47}{1000}Q,}
\tag{39}
\]
while in the degree-weighted dominant branch
\(M_{\mathrm{dom}}^d\geq P_{\mathrm{tar}}/2\),
\[
 \boxed{\mathfrak A_d>\frac{73}{1600}Q.}
\tag{40}
\]
In the complementary square branches, (31)-(33) give, respectively,
globally halfspace-dominated selectable clouds of mass strictly larger than
\(49\gamma_dQ/200\) and \(381\gamma_dQ/1600\).

Finally, the degree-weighted construction is an exact extension of the
accepted off-diagonal product rematching, not merely a second choice of
notation.  Let
\[
 L_\xi:=\sum_{m\equiv\xi}d_m=2M_{d,\xi}.
\tag{41}
\]
For \(L_\xi>0\), accepted fact `7ab0a03cf9189637` defines
\[
 q_{\{u,v\}}^{\mathrm{prod}}:=\frac{d_ud_v}{L_\xi}
 \qquad(u\ne v,\ u\equiv v\equiv\xi).
\tag{42}
\]
For every target \(t\), the degree-weighted orbit masses obey
\[
 \boxed{
 \beta_{d,\xi,t,[h]}=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\frac{d_t^2}{2L_\xi},&[h]=[0],\\[3mm]
 q_{\{t+h,t-h\}}^{\mathrm{prod}},&[h]\ne[0],
 \end{cases}}
\tag{43}
\]
and hence
\[
 \boxed{
 B_{d,\xi,t}
 =\frac{d_t^2}{2L_\xi}
 +\sum_{\substack{f=\{u,v\}\in\operatorname{supp}q^{\mathrm{prod}}\\
 u\equiv v\equiv\xi,\ (u+v)/2=t}}
 q_f^{\mathrm{prod}}.}
\tag{44}
\]
The corresponding first-moment identity is
\[
 \boxed{
 B_{d,\xi,t}p_{d,\xi,t}
 =\frac{d_t^2}{2L_\xi}c_t
 +\sum_{\substack{f=\{u,v\}\in\operatorname{supp}q^{\mathrm{prod}}\\
 u\equiv v\equiv\xi,\ (u+v)/2=t}}
 q_f^{\mathrm{prod}}\frac{c_u+c_v}{2}}
\tag{45}
\]
whenever \(B_{d,\xi,t}>0\), with a missing loop interpreted as zero.
Thus the extra mass in this specialization consists exactly of diagonal
loops; no off-diagonal product edge is altered.

No conclusion above bounds the residual rank of either cloud, absorbs either
affine defect into an existing terminal capacity, closes the independent
positive-fresh branch, or proves the locked weak Oertel conjecture.
